title: Seated Leg Curl
summary: A machine leg curl sitting up, so the hamstrings work with the hips bent and stay long. The app's main hamstring isolation: hamstrings 1.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: seated leg curl machine or attachment.

muscles.why: The hamstrings bend the knee. Three of the four also cross the hip; sitting bends the hip and lengthens them, so they work from a longer length than in a lying curl.

region_notes.text: Seated leg curls grew the hamstrings more than lying leg curls in a 12-week study.

setup.text: Line your knees up with the machine's pivot.
Lower pad just above the heels, thigh pad snug so your hips can't lift.
Hold the handles and sit tall, then lean forward a little.

form_cues.why: Leaning forward bends the hip more, lengthening the hamstrings further.

form_cues.cue: Curl the pad down and under
form_cues.why: Pull the heels down and back under the seat.
Nearly straight at the top keeps the muscle long at the start of each rep.

form_cues.cue: Leaning forward adds stretch. Research suggests seated curls build more than lying curls.
form_cues.why: The tip reflects the seated-vs-lying study cited above.
Coaches find it easier to keep tension on the hamstrings this way; not tested for growth.

bias_tweaks.effect: More hip flexion, so the hamstrings are longer throughout.
bias_tweaks.caveat: The extra lean has not been tested on its own.

bias_tweaks.change: Finish hard sets with partials near straight legs
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps working in the lengthened range after full reps run out.
bias_tweaks.caveat: The edge for lengthened partials across studies is small and uncertain.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Letting the weight snap back up between reps.
mistakes.fix: Control the return to nearly straight legs; reduce the load if the stack slams.

mistakes.text: Thigh pad too loose, so the hips rise.
mistakes.fix: Snug the pad before the first set.

mistakes.text: Short reps that never reach the stretch.
mistakes.fix: Return to nearly straight legs every rep.

misconceptions.myth: Lying and seated curls are interchangeable.
misconceptions.reality: Seated curls grew the hamstrings more, likely because the hip is bent and the muscle is longer.

misconceptions.myth: Machines don't build muscle like free weights.
misconceptions.reality: Free-weight and machine training gave similar muscle growth in a meta-analysis. Pick by fit, stability and how well you can push close to failure.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Machine curls are easy to push close to failure; stop when the hips lift or the range shrinks.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: One leg at a time to even out sides.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: No machine; very hard eccentric hamstring work. Start with assisted or partial reps.
Trains the hamstrings at the hip instead of the knee, with a long stretch.
Hip and knee work together, with more total load and fatigue.

notes: The seated-vs-lying finding is from one 12-week study.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
